activation: Routes and namespaced authorization abilities are registered in source. The default-disabled feature gate prevents availability; production activation still requires a separate release approval.
activation_prerequisites: The V2 controllers and route table are registered in source behind EnsureTransmittalV2Enabled; transmittal_v2.enabled defaults false. Production activation remains a separately approved release decision.

All three V2 controllers use the V2-only EnsureTransmittalV2Enabled middleware, which reads transmittal_v2.enabled (default false); upload and acknowledgment actions also retain their method-level feature checks.
The registered provider defines only transmittal-v2.* abilities. It does not map the shared Transmittal model globally to TransmittalV2Policy.
V2 JS/CSS and file-tools entries are configured locally; an isolated temporary-output build passed. Verify the staging build artifact, manifest, release path and deployment hook before activation.
Keep the isolated MySQL compatibility and concurrency gate blocked until a disposable MySQL environment is verified.
route_order_note: Place static routes such as /create, /smart-upload, /analyze, and /uploads before /{transmittal} routes to avoid dynamic-route capture.
csrf: All state-changing browser forms and fetch requests use the web middleware CSRF token. Do not exempt these routes.

endpoint_security_review.csrf: All 32 endpoints use web middleware; browser mutations require CSRF. Local mock events use timestamped HMAC; the isolated Brevo branch uses a configured Bearer secret and bounded, replay-keyed provider evidence.
endpoint_security_review.authorization: Each route records an authentication model and authorization rule; authenticated actions use auth middleware, while documented guest flows require scoped session ownership or expiring recipient tokens.
endpoint_security_review.throttling: All minimum-release state-changing endpoints have explicit throttles; tokenized public endpoints remain throttled.
endpoint_security_review.activation: Registered in source behind the default-disabled V2 feature gate; production activation remains separately gated.
